summary: Dulundur is four valleys of orc clans under the Four Fires: iron of the hills, no yoke for the hall, the Free Moot, an answer to the envoys from the south, and a war for the holds.

dulgashs_law_spirit.name: Dulgash's Law
dulgashs_law_spirit.desc: Chief Dulgash's word is law in the four valleys, and the hearth-keepers make sure that his word is heard. It is rough justice, and it is quick.

one_hall.name: One Chief, One Hall
one_hall.desc: The four hearths have agreed to speak through one mouth, and the mouth is Dulgash's. A hold with a single voice is harder to split than one that must be asked.

valleys_speak.name: The Valleys Speak
valleys_speak.desc: Each valley keeps its own hearth and sends its own voice to the hall. Decisions take longer, and once taken are not broken.

iron_trade.name: Iron for Blackton
iron_trade.desc: Dulundur iron goes to the five towns by the cartload, and the harbour silver comes back the same way. Both sides are the richer for it.

hills_provide.name: The Hills Provide
hills_provide.desc: Iron, charcoal and hands to work them: the hills have never been short of any of them. A well-supplied hold builds fast and does not complain.

proud_hold.name: The Proud Hold
proud_hold.desc: Dulundur remembers who built Goldoroth and how, and has resolved to be neither its tool nor its supper. The pride is old, and it holds.

first_among_holds.name: First Among the Holds
first_among_holds.desc: Dulundur's voice carries at the Moot, and the small halls look to it for a lead. A leader of equals is trusted for as long as he does not forget it.

hill_watch.name: Whispers in the Hills
hill_watch.desc: Spies and listeners are placed in every valley and on every pass. A word spoken against the hall is known before supper.

war_drums.name: War-Drums of Dulundur
war_drums.desc: The drums of the four valleys beat a single rhythm that carries across a battlefield. A host that fights to a common beat does not lose heart.

defiance.name: Defiance
defiance.desc: Dulundur has refused the Iron Yoke and the black banner, and the whole hold knows what the refusal will cost. They fight the way a cornered thing fights.

the_four_fires.title: The Four Fires Are Lit
the_four_fires.desc: From the four valleys the clan fires climb into the dusk, and the chiefs gather in the great hall to hear Dulgash. He has asked each of them to say what the hold needs most, and he has promised to listen.

options.name: Let the Chief speak for all.

envoys_at_the_fires.title: Envoys at the Fires
envoys_at_the_fires.desc: Strangers from Nafeher sit at the hall's fire and speak of spoils in the north and old friendships. The chiefs laugh, or do not, and Grushka of the Four Fires watches the faces of those who do not.

peace_of_the_hills.title: Peace of the Hills
peace_of_the_hills.desc: A messenger in Dulundur colours has come to Cocanoor under a white pennant. He says that the hills are not worth another winter's fighting, and that Dulundur will gladly take back its dead.

options.name: The hills are not worth it.

the_hills_answer.title: The Hills Answer
the_hills_answer.desc: The Warking's banners are seen going north, and the passes are quiet. Cocanoor has gone home, and Dulundur is still Dulundur.

focuses.name: The Four Fires
focuses.desc: Four valleys, four hearths, one hall: when Chief Dulgash speaks, each fire sends an ember to the hall's great hearth. The Four Fires burn together only a few times a year, and the clans remember each of them.

focuses.name: Chiefs of the Four Valleys
focuses.desc: The chiefs of the four valleys sit at Dulgash's table in order of age, and each swears the hall's oath in his own words. They leave with a charge, a gift and an extra spear or two.

focuses.name: Dulgash's Law
focuses.desc: Dulgash sets down a few plain laws in the hall: no blood-feud within the four valleys, no hearth turned away, no debt left unpaid. They are cut into the doorposts so that no one can claim not to have seen them.

focuses.name: One Chief, One Hall
focuses.desc: The valleys agree to let one chief speak for all of them, and that chief is Dulgash. The hearth-keepers give up their old right to veto, and the hall grows quicker and harder.

focuses.name: The Valleys Speak
focuses.desc: The valleys decide instead that no one chief shall decide. Each hearth sends a voice to the hall, and Dulgash must win them over one at a time.

focuses.name: The Pride of Dulundur
focuses.desc: Dulundur's chiefs have a name for the feeling that rises in them when Cocanoor sends its gifts. It is pride, and it is also the thing that has kept the four valleys free.

focuses.name: Iron of the Hills
focuses.desc: Dulundur sits on seams of dark iron, which the clans have dug for more winters than anyone has counted. The hall decides to dig deeper and to sell what it digs to those who pay fairly.

focuses.name: Ore Roads
focuses.desc: Rough tracks are widened into ore roads, with stone beds and timber culverts. A wagon of iron can reach the harbour in half the time it once took.

focuses.name: The Deep Pits
focuses.desc: The old pits are cleared of rubble and sunk another fifty paces. Ozgar Ironhand, the Pit-Master, drives the diggers hard and feeds them well.

focuses.name: Iron for Blackton
focuses.desc: A long road of iron wagons leaves the hills for the harbour towns, guarded and counted at each stage. Blackton pays in silver and in friendship.

focuses.name: Hall Forges
focuses.desc: Forges are raised inside the hall's own walls, and their smoke blackens the roof-beams. A blade made there carries the hall's mark, and the mark is worth money.

focuses.name: The Hills Provide
focuses.desc: Mines, roads and forges are drawn into a single plan. What the hills provide, the hall uses, and nothing is wasted.

focuses.name: No Yoke for Dulundur
focuses.desc: Cocanoor's envoys speak of a light yoke, a fair tithe and a seat at the Warking's table. Dulgash listens, thanks them for the wine and has the chains they brought as gifts hung up as a curiosity.

focuses.name: Send Back the Gifts
focuses.desc: The gifts of black iron are loaded onto the same carts that brought them and sent north, with a courteous note. Cocanoor receives them in silence.

focuses.name: Hill Forts
focuses.desc: Stone forts rise on the heads of the valleys, built by the clans and manned by their sons. Whatever comes through the passes will meet iron first.

focuses.name: The Proud Hold
focuses.desc: Dulundur declares itself a proud hold, beholden to none and frightened of none. The declaration is read in every valley and shouted at the passes.

focuses.name: The Hall Answers No One
focuses.desc: The Four Fires are lit and Dulgash stands before them. The hall answers no master, he says, and the war-drums begin to beat.

focuses.name: Speak to the Holds
focuses.desc: Dulundur sends envoys with gifts of iron to every free hold in the Dark Lands. They carry a simple message: we are not alone in our refusal, and need not stand alone.

focuses.name: The Moot Stone
focuses.desc: A stone is raised on the high moor between the valleys, and the free holds are called to gather at it. Dulundur is the first to speak, and the first to listen.

focuses.name: Gifts to the Small Halls
focuses.desc: The small halls are the first that Cocanoor will swallow, so Dulundur sends them barley, iron and a quiet promise. The gifts are small and well-timed, and they matter.

focuses.name: First Among the Holds
focuses.desc: At the Moot, Dulundur's voice is heard first, and the others look to it for the sign. Dulgash holds up a hand, and the room falls quiet.

focuses.name: The Moot Rides
focuses.desc: When Cocanoor moves against any of the Moot's holds, every drum in the free Dark Lands begins to beat. Dulundur's sons ride out to meet the threat, and the Moot rides with them.

focuses.name: Envoys at the Fires
focuses.desc: Strangers from Nafeher arrive at the hall with gifts of silver and sweet words. The chiefs listen and say little, and the hearth-keepers watch the strangers' hands.

focuses.name: Send Them South
focuses.desc: Dulgash has the envoys escorted to the southern pass, and the gifts, unopened, escorted after them. The chiefs laugh, or they do not.

focuses.name: The Price of Spoils
focuses.desc: Some chiefs say that the strangers offer what Dulundur lacks: arms, silver and a promise of spoils from the northern wars. The price is not discussed in the hall, and that is the worry.

focuses.name: Whispers in the Hills
focuses.desc: Whatever the hall decided about the envoys, it now keeps listeners on every pass. Nothing is said in the Dark Lands that Dulundur does not hear within a week.

focuses.name: Warbands of Dulundur
focuses.desc: The clans raise warbands under their own chiefs, and each warband carries its own banner and its own boast. In the field they are loud and in the line they are steady.

focuses.name: Hill Runners
focuses.desc: Light bowmen run the high ridges with short horn bows, loosing three arrows to every breath. They are hard to catch and harder to ignore.

focuses.name: Shields of the Four Valleys
focuses.desc: Each valley paints its shields with its own sign, and the signs are known on every field of the Dark Lands. A man will not run from his own valley's shield.

focuses.name: War-Drums of Dulundur
focuses.desc: The drums of the four valleys are tuned to a common beat, and drummers are trained to hold it against any din. A host that marches to a steady drum does not stray.

focuses.name: Defy Cocanoor
focuses.desc: The Warking's host has crossed the border, and Dulundur's answer is the Four Fires lit on every ridge. Whatever Cocanoor wanted, it will have to take with iron.

focuses.name: Every Hall a Fortress
focuses.desc: Every hall in the four valleys is made ready for siege: gates barred, wells covered, a store of arrows in each loft. The chiefs sleep in their armour.

focuses.name: The Moot Answers
focuses.desc: Dulundur sends riders to every hold of the Moot with a single message: the Warking has struck, and the Moot is called. Drums begin to answer from the farthest hills.

focuses.name: Strike the Tributaries
focuses.desc: The tributaries of Cocanoor lie open along Dulundur's border, held by garrisons that did not choose their master. Some of the chiefs say that a blow struck there would be a blow struck for freedom.

focuses.name: Peace of the Hills
focuses.desc: With the cores held and the passes closed, Dulgash sends a messenger to Cocanoor under a white pennant. The hills are not worth another winter of fighting, he says, and the Warking is welcome to agree.

focuses.name: The Hold Endures
focuses.desc: The war is over, and the four valleys are still four valleys. The Fires are lit one by one, and the clans eat together for the first time in a year.
